name: Revvity, Inc.

profile.description: Revvity, Inc. (formerly PerkinElmer) is a global health sciences company providing diagnostics, life sciences solutions, and applied services. In 2023, the company completed a transformative $2.45B divestiture of its food, environment, and applied businesses, rebranding as Revvity to focus exclusively on health sciences [3]. CEO Prahlad Singh (since 2019) leads 11,000 employees across two segments: Diagnostics (immunodiagnostics, reproductive health, applied genomics) and Life Sciences (instruments, reagents, software for drug discovery). Q2 2026 revenue was $730M with adjusted EPS of $1.41; full-year 2026 guidance is $2.83-$2.86B in revenue with 4-5% organic growth and adjusted EPS of $5.30-$5.40 [1]. The company is divesting its China Immunodiagnostics unit for up to $200M and positioning in GLP-1/obesity testing markets. Market cap approximately $16B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Revvity executed a significant strategic transformation — divesting legacy PerkinElmer food and environmental testing businesses for $2.45B in 2023 to focus entirely on health sciences, then rebranding as Revvity [3]. This pivot opened a new, focused growth trajectory in diagnostics and life sciences. The ongoing China Immunodiagnostics divestiture ($200M) and entry into GLP-1/obesity testing represent continued portfolio refinement [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Revvity has deployed AI-enabled learning platforms and AI-driven technologies across its diagnostics operations, with leadership noting AI investments support long-term revenue growth [3]. However, no specific AI revenue figures or quantified cost savings have been publicly reported. Market Share Leadership (1/2): Revvity is a meaningful player in the diagnostics and life sciences instruments market, though not a dominant category leader. The Diagnostics segment is delivering double-digit growth, and the company has established positions in reproductive health and neonatal screening [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The GLP-1/obesity testing opportunity represents a pipeline catalyst — analysts recently hiked price targets citing this positioning [1]. However, specific next-gen product launches with named timelines and revenue visibility are limited. R&D Intensity (1/1): As a health sciences company, Revvity's R&D spending is at or above industry average, supporting continued instrument and reagent development across both segments.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Revvity's purpose — advancing health sciences solutions and technologies — is clear and specific to healthcare, identifying what the company does and for whom [3]. The divestiture of non-healthcare businesses demonstrates commitment to this focused mission. However, the purpose is not distinctive enough to differentiate from dozens of healthcare peers with similar 'improving health outcomes' missions. Community & Charitable Impact (1/2): Revvity published its inaugural ESG report in 2023, is a signatory to the UN Global Compact, and has committed to a 50% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2033 — demonstrating general corporate responsibility commitment with specific environmental targets [3]. Employee Retention & Tenure (0/2): Glassdoor reviews are mixed — some employees praise collaboration and innovation culture, while others cite low pay relative to biotech peers and management issues [3]. No specific turnover or tenure data is publicly available to confirm above-average retention. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by CEO Prahlad Singh or other executives was identified during the research period.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on all seven Growth metrics. D/E of 46.2% is well within the 70% target, scoring perfectly and reflecting conservative leverage post-divestiture [4]. Forward P/E of 24.32 and PEG of 0.73 are the infrastructure highlights — the PEG in particular (below 1.0 with 2x weight) indicates the market is pricing Revvity for attractive growth relative to earnings expansion [4]. However, ROE of just 3.2% (target 15%) scores poorly at 0.21, reflecting the post-transformation earnings ramp that has not yet reached full potential. Revenue growth YoY of 1.3% significantly underperforms the 10% target. The 5-year revenue CAGR of -4.8% ($3,312M in 2022 to $2,856M in 2025) is distorted by the PerkinElmer divestiture — organic growth post-rebrand is approximately 2% annually [1]. Profit margin of 8.2% is below the 20% target, reflecting the company's transition-stage profitability. The stock easily clears the liquidity floor at ~$245M daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Revvity's core business — manufacturing diagnostic instruments, reagents, and detection technologies for healthcare and life sciences — is structurally protected from AI disruption [3]. Physical laboratory instruments, consumable reagents, and regulated diagnostic workflows require specialized manufacturing, quality control, and regulatory approvals (FDA, CE-IVD) that AI cannot replicate or displace. The Diagnostics segment's immunodiagnostics, reproductive health screening, and neonatal testing involve regulated clinical processes with high switching costs. Life Sciences instruments for drug discovery require precision hardware and validated assay protocols. AI may enhance analytical capabilities (image analysis, data interpretation) but cannot substitute for the physical instruments and consumable reagents that generate recurring revenue. The company's positioning in GLP-1/obesity testing further insulates it, as these testing workflows require specialized diagnostic platforms [1]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Revvity is deploying AI-enabled platforms across its diagnostics operations and has identified AI-driven technologies as a growth driver, indicating early-stage AI revenue contribution through enhanced instrument analytics and automated workflows [3].

infinite_game.summary: Revvity demonstrates meaningful infinite-game qualities, particularly in the courage shown by divesting $2.45B in legacy PerkinElmer businesses to focus on a health sciences cause — a painful short-term revenue reduction for long-term strategic clarity [3]. The PerkinElmer-to-Revvity transformation is a genuine example of existential flexibility, though it was partly market-driven (food and environmental testing were underperforming). The company has a genuine healthcare mission and organizational stability under CEO Singh's 7+ year tenure. However, the competitive language remains financially focused, Glassdoor reviews suggest mixed organizational trust, and the company has not yet proven this new identity through a major crisis or market disruption.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Revvity's purpose — advancing health sciences solutions to improve human health outcomes — is genuine, distinctive (post-divestiture), and partially lived through the decision to divest profitable but off-mission businesses [3]. The PerkinElmer-to-Revvity transformation demonstrates that strategic decisions trace back to the healthcare focus. However, the company is only 3 years into this focused identity, and the cause has not been tested through crisis or multi-decade consistency. The divestiture of the China Immunodiagnostics unit suggests ongoing portfolio refinement in service of the cause [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Revvity has leadership stability with CEO Prahlad Singh serving since 2019 (7+ years) and a management team with stated commitment to collaboration and innovation [3]. Some Glassdoor reviews describe a supportive workplace with investment in technology. However, other reviews cite low pay relative to biotech peers, insufficient staffing, and management decisions perceived as disconnected from operational reality. The mixed employee sentiment suggests adequate but not exceptional organizational trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No specific evidence of an infinite competitive mindset. Revvity's competitive language in earnings calls and corporate materials is focused on market positioning and portfolio optimization rather than learning from competitors' strengths [1]. The company competes with Thermo Fisher Scientific, Danaher, and Roche Diagnostics but no public commentary references these as worthy rivals that inspire self-improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The PerkinElmer-to-Revvity transformation represents meaningful strategic evolution — divesting $2.45B in food, environmental, and applied testing businesses to focus entirely on health sciences [3]. This was a deliberate narrowing of the company's scope that reduced revenue but improved strategic focus. The ongoing China Immunodiagnostics divestiture continues this trend. However, the pivot was incremental (entering adjacent healthcare markets, not a fundamentally new business model) and partly driven by market underperformance in divested segments rather than a transformative cause-driven vision.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The decision to divest $2.45B in legacy PerkinElmer businesses required courage — walking away from established revenue streams and a 85-year brand name to focus on a smaller, more specialized health sciences portfolio [3]. CEO Singh chose long-term strategic clarity over short-term revenue maximization. The company has also invested in GLP-1 testing capabilities before the market fully developed. However, the divestiture was financially supported (proceeds de-levered the balance sheet) and the rebranding was also motivated by the PerkinElmer name's association with legacy businesses.

investment_thesis: Revvity at 24.3x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.73 represents a post-transformation healthcare platform trading at a discount to its growth trajectory — the Diagnostics segment is delivering double-digit revenue and margin expansion, analysts have recently hiked price targets citing GLP-1/obesity testing opportunities, and full-year 2026 guidance of $5.30-$5.40 adjusted EPS represents meaningful earnings improvement [1]. The $2.45B PerkinElmer divestiture created a focused health sciences company with D/E of just 46.2%, a clean balance sheet, and growing organic revenue of 4-5% [4]. The China Immunodiagnostics divestiture ($200M) further sharpens the portfolio. Tariff-related refunds of $16M in Q2 bolstered near-term margins, and the recurring reagent/consumables business provides revenue visibility.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on sluggish growth and post-transformation execution risk. Revenue growth YoY of just 1.3% and GAAP profit margin of 8.2% indicate Revvity has not yet reached escape velocity from its transformation — adjusted metrics look better but GAAP remains weak [4]. ROE of 3.2% is far below the 15% target, reflecting that the company has significant capital deployed but isn't yet generating commensurate returns. The Life Sciences segment is underperforming with softer results, offset only by Diagnostics strength. The 5-year revenue CAGR of -4.8% (distorted by the divestiture) signals that the old PerkinElmer was a declining business, and it's not yet clear whether the new Revvity can sustain the Diagnostics growth trajectory. Trailing P/E of 68.9x is very expensive on a GAAP basis. The GLP-1 testing opportunity is real but early-stage and faces competition from Thermo Fisher and Danaher [1]. The China divestiture reduces geographic diversification at a time when healthcare demand in Asia is growing.
key_catalysts: GLP-1/obesity drug testing opportunity could accelerate Diagnostics segment growth as Revvity positions its immunodiagnostics platforms to serve the expanding weight-loss pharmaceutical market — analysts recently hiked targets citing this catalyst [1]

Adjusted EPS trajectory from $1.18 (Q2 2025) to $1.41 (Q2 2026) suggests operating leverage is building — if this pace continues, the company could reach $6+ adjusted EPS in FY2027, driving PEG-based re-rating [1]
China Immunodiagnostics divestiture ($200M) closes in 2026-2027, providing capital for strategic reinvestment and further portfolio optimization in higher-growth health sciences verticals [1]
key_risks: Life Sciences segment weakness could accelerate if academic and pharmaceutical R&D spending contracts, offsetting Diagnostics strength and causing organic growth to fall below the 4-5% guidance range [1]

GAAP profitability remains weak with 8.2% profit margin and 3.2% ROE — if adjusted-to-GAAP convergence does not materialize, the stock's premium valuation (68.9x trailing P/E) becomes increasingly difficult to justify [4]
Competition from Thermo Fisher Scientific and Danaher in diagnostic instruments and GLP-1 testing could limit Revvity's share gains in its highest-growth addressable markets [3]
